questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Djibouti?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Djibouti on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Geography” part of the Djibouti article.

questions.proof: It is bordered by Eritrea in the north, Ethiopia in the west and south, and Awdal of Somalia in the southeast.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Djibouti?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Djiboutians” part of the Djibouti article.

questions.proof: It has many languages - though Somali and Afar are the most widely spoken ones, Arabic and French serve as the official languages.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “The history of Djibouti goes back thousands of years when it was part of the Sabean Empire (_____) to a time when Djiboutians traded hides and skins for the perfumes and spices of ancient Egypt, Pakistan, and China.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “Empire”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “History” part of the Djibouti article.

questions.proof: The history of Djibouti goes back thousands of years when it was part of the Sabean Empire (Ethiopia) to a time when Djiboutians traded hides and skins for the perfumes and spices of ancient Egypt, Pakistan, and China.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Djibouti gained its independence from _____ on June 27, 1977.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “independence”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Djibouti article.

questions.proof: Djibouti gained its independence from France on June 27, 1977.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “There is a small Djiboutian diaspora in North America, Europe, and _____.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “Europe”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Djiboutians” part of the Djibouti article.

questions.proof: There is a small Djiboutian diaspora in North America, Europe, and Australia.
